title: Two architectures for letting agents analyse business data
friendlyTitle: A safer way for AI agents to work with company data
summary: Database researcher Daniel Abadi compares giving an agent direct access to separate databases with putting a data-virtualisation layer between the agent and those systems. He argues that the intermediate layer can improve cross-source joins, governance and efficiency, while adding upfront cost and complexity.
friendlySummary: This article compares two ways to connect an AI agent to several databases. A shared data layer may make access easier to control and queries more efficient.
whyItMatters: Businesses connecting agents to internal data must decide where permissions, query optimisation and shared context live. The useful design question is not simply whether an agent can query a database, but how to limit cost and risk while preserving enough context for a sound answer.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Giving an agent direct access to every database can be costly and risky. A controlled middle layer can help a business manage access and combine data.
